Notes for the controller:
1. Root cause confirmed from both eval records: not data volume (unified files total ~270KB) but one long-lived boot subagent accumulating persona + walked-step context and re-sending it every turn. Fresh single-purpose subagents per step, reading only their own step file plus specific data files, is the fix. Expected profile: tens of thousands of input tokens per step instead of 500-720k — inside the 1-1.5M/boot target once step-01.2's 82-719k also drops.
2. One functional simplification worth knowing: step-04 no longer re-calls Clay MCP — it reads `data/clay-reminders-unified.json` (step-01.2 Pull C already covers the same 7-day window; the "always attempt" mandate stays at the pull step). If you want a fresh Clay attempt at step-04 anyway, that's a one-line revert.
3. Per-step guardrail verifiers (step-02/03/04 `.py`) key on data-file presence and state.yaml accumulated-context — the rewrite preserves both contracts, so the deterministic step guardrails run unchanged.
4. Harvest encoded: Edit-not-Bash attribution rule, minimal step frontmatter (err-20261013T151635-DORL18 — no run outputs in frontmatter, everything to state.yaml), and the no-walking rule with eval evidence cited in each step file so the reasoning survives future edits.
